I kind of understand the dilemma that producers have. If I invest 80 million dollars into a project, that project better make some god damned money. It's not bad to want a yield on the return of your investment. That's just business. The problem is the desire for guaranteeing the ROI has dramatically impacted writers and directors ability to innovate.

Doing a remake almost always outputs more than is put in. If it wasn't a safe bet, people would stop doing it. Consumers are partially to blame on this. The new Star Wars did a remarkable job of innovating nothing while experiencing wonderful box office success, and that only worsens the problem. Avatar at least explored 3d technology, although the plot was extremely lackluster. When original movies come out, they're not getting massive blockbuster success, but a Mad Max remake will.

Writers are scared of trying new things, so plots have become increasingly predictable and stupid. They're terrified about even glossing over anything remotely controversial these days, and with good reason. If I input a transgender person into a story, and they experience any form of conflict, my family is likely to receive death threats from SJWs.

I don't know what the correct solution is. What I would enjoy though, is more opportunity for lesser known directors to enjoy their spot in the limelight. If the Sundance Film Festival doesn't get broadcast nationally already, then it is time to start. More cinemas should feature opportunities to watch films the local college kids are making. And the IFC needs a more dominant online presence.

Dungeon Raiders 2 - Let's Play Two Games

I played two games of "Dungeon Raiders 2": a four player game and a nine player game.

Here's a rough overview of the game play:

I play a dungeon raider who is trying to make the most money. I'm traveling from room to room deciding if I want to leave or stay.

If I leave, I grab the remaining gems on the way back to the entrance (splitting everything with anybody else who leaves). Leaving also keeps my gems safe.

If I stay, I risk my gems for more gems.

Various adventures with slightly different rules can show up in each dungeon. There are currently 8 adventures: Lava Lake (pay to stay), Mushrooms (alter your share), Sphinx (split path), Banker (gems into cash), Sun/Moon (1 vs 2 gems), Monkey (steals 25% of your gems), Scout (tells you where the spider is), and Three Card Monte (find the best card).

You can get the game for free right now at http://darkinfinitysoftware.com/dungeonraiders2/.

Edit: I wanted to add that you can also play this on Android. It's okay on a Nexus 7. I'm working on a 4 Player mode with larger buttons in each player's area.
